Docs/ Theme development/Theme File Editor

Theme File Editor

Edit templates and CSS in the admin without recompiling, and where the overlay directory lives.

Appearance › Theme File Editor opens any installed theme's templates, stylesheets and scripts in the browser, as in WordPress — bundled themes included, although their Go glue (theme_<slug>.go) is compiled and cannot be edited.

How it works

Theme files are read through an overlay: the server first looks in <data>/themes/<slug>/<path> (WPGO_THEMES_DIR, the themes volume in Docker), then in the copy embedded in the binary or, for packages, the installed package directory. Saving a file in the editor writes it to the overlay, re-parses the theme's template set and test-renders a page. If the save produces a template or render error it is rolled back automatically and the editor shows the error, so the site never serves a broken page.

Restore original deletes the overlay file, bringing back the embedded or packaged version. Assets (style.css, js/…) saved in the overlay are served with Cache-Control: no-cache, so browsers revalidate and pick up the change.

For a theme package, the overlay directory and the package directory are the same, so edits are edits of the installed files.

Editing on disk

Anything you put under WPGO_THEMES_DIR/<slug>/ is picked up the same way; templates are parsed on the next request. This is the quickest loop while developing a package: point WPGO_THEMES_DIR at your working copy and edit with your editor.

Turning it off

WPGO_DISALLOW_FILE_EDIT=1 makes the editor read-only (WordPress' DISALLOW_FILE_EDIT); the overlay still applies to files already there. The editor requires the edit_themes capability (administrators).

What you cannot edit

Theme glue written in Go, theme.json semantics (widget areas, menu locations, Customizer controls — re-upload the package for those), and plugins: the Plugin File Editor only shows packages, since plugin code is compiled WebAssembly.
